audits.text:
## 49a0b77dcc7f

**Reproduced domain and override defects.** Generator version 3.0.1, SHA-256 `e58fc2502004e799029304e70c3c6c9f19fa0ce854070080bdc0cc9bf34859a6`; canonical rule hash `f4456992bd53`.

The canonical zero-marker case has `k = 0` and selects the solid zero-hole color-7 object. The selected validator rejects that exact canonical input with `no color-1 marker cells in row 0 (k undefined)`. The supported Racket application executes it successfully and returns the published `2×3` solid-7 crop. Across 600 defaults (200 each easy/medium/hard), the generator emitted **0** zero-marker cases, so this is a real canonical-support gap rather than a rare sampled omission.

The exact-control contract is also reproduced as broken. At seed 123, sample index 4, hard difficulty, requesting `grid_h=10`, `grid_w=14`, `k_count=1`, and `n_objects=2` produced `17×25`, five markers, and five color-7 components; `self_check` still returned `[]`. The five-marker result also exceeds the advertised/invariant maximum of four. Evidence: `checks/audit/49a0b77dcc7f/probe.json`, exact canonical input `input.json`, and authoritative receipt `racket.json`.

**Disposition:** actionable reproduced defects. Add k=0/zero-hole support; route all advertised controls through exact draws; make the validator enforce marker range, component count, unique hole counts, and existence/uniqueness of the selected object.
